newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African golds fall to close, trade seen subdued.
newsitem.headline: S.African golds fall to close, trade seen subdued.

text.p: South African gold shares closed Monday's quiet trade far down, bashed by a weak bullion price, expectations of poor first quarter gold mine results and worry about a possible U.S. rate hike, dealers said.
The bullion price held slightly above the key $350 an ounce level for much of the day before falling through and was last trading at $349.10/60 an ounce.

Dealers said that the first quarter gold reporting round, kicking off on April 17 with Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd, was likely to be disappointing due to the soft dollar gold price, firmer rand and four public holidays in the period.
Tuesday's Federal reserve meeting, at which Governor Alan Greenspan was largely expected to hike U.S. interest rates by 0.25 percentage points, was also sparking nerves.
Greg Amoils, portfolio manager at Irish & Co, added that in the event of Greenspan not raising rates, local industrial shares could even enjoy some firming.
"Any strong or reasonable factor could influence the market strongly. If Greenspan doesn't raise rates then our industrials could see a little run up," he said.

Otherwise, trade on Monday was subdued, and seen hushed for the rest of the week, by vacation fever ahead of the Good Friday and Easter Monday holidays as players relinquished positions for closed markets, dealers said.
They added that the local industrial board was well-supported and unlikely to shrink much in this quiet trade.
"Johannesburg is being very resilient. As much as you hit it, it's not coming off," a dealer said.
Gold shares fell 56.4 points to 1,326.0, industrials hopped 5.7 points to 8,328.4 and all-shares dipped 9.6 points to 7,088.9 points.
